Egyptian officials say approximately 95% of output is intended for export, capitalizing on Egypt's access to European, African and Middle Eastern markets via the adjacent Suez Canal. The deal was announced during Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit to Egypt in early September 2026 — his first in a decade — during which Beijing and Cairo signed more than twenty cooperation documents spanning trade, industry and technology.

The Sokhna project adds to a growing cluster of Chinese manufacturing investment inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone's TEDA sub-zone, which by the end of 2025 had attracted nearly 200 companies and roughly $3.8 billion in cumulative investment, and which officials say will expand into a 'Phase 3' covering renewable energy, batteries and additional automotive component manufacturing. Egypt signed its Belt and Road Initiative memorandum of understanding with China in January 2016.

Name: UAE Dubai World Central Airport Aviation Complex (China Railway Construction Corporation)
Description:
On May 18, 2026, China Railway Construction Corporation Limited (CRCC) began construction on a major aviation engineering and maintenance complex for Emirates Airline and Group at Dubai World Central (Al Maktoum International Airport) in southern Dubai. CRCC's unit won the bid for the engineering-facilities contract at a value Reuters reported at approximately $4.77 billion (about AED 17.5 billion), while Xinhua and CRCC cited total project investment exceeding $5 billion.

The complex comprises eight maintenance hangars and two paint hangars across roughly 1.1 million square metres, with capacity to service up to 28 wide-body aircraft simultaneously — CRCC and Emirates describe it as one of the largest projects of its kind in the world. Completion is targeted for mid-2030. CRCC's chairman called the project 'an important milestone in high-quality Belt and Road cooperation' between China and the UAE.

The project extends China's growing footprint in Gulf aviation and logistics infrastructure alongside existing BRI-linked UAE projects such as the Abu Dhabi–Dubai high-speed rail line and COSCO's Khalifa Port CSP terminal. The UAE signed a memorandum of understanding on Belt and Road cooperation with China in 2018.

Name: Peru Chancay–Sierra Central Railway (PowerChina)
Description:
In January 2026, Peru's government awarded Power Construction Corporation of China (PowerChina) a $420 million engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract to build a 120-kilometre railway linking the Port of Chancay — the COSCO Shipping-operated megaport on Peru's central coast — with the mineral-rich central highland regions of Junín, Huancavelica and Pasco. The award, reported by La República and Infobae in January 2026, drew scrutiny in Washington over deepening Chinese influence in Peruvian infrastructure.

The line will cross the Andes via tunnels, viaducts and extensive earthworks, cutting transport times for copper and other strategic minerals from over 18 hours by road to roughly five hours by rail, according to Peruvian officials. Construction is expected to take about 36 months, with service entry targeted around 2028. The EPC contract covers design and construction only; operations and maintenance are to be handled separately.

The railway is designed to feed export cargo directly into the Chancay megaport, which held its first-phase inauguration on November 14, 2024 as part of a $3.5 billion, COSCO Shipping-led project already tracked on this site as one of Latin America's largest BRI-linked assets. Peru signed its Belt and Road Initiative memorandum of understanding with China in 2019, the same year COSCO acquired its majority stake in the Chancay port.

Name: Tanzania Standard Gauge Railway Lot 6 – Tabora–Kigoma (CRCC/CCECC)
Description:
On August 5, 2026, Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan laid the foundation stone in Kigoma launching construction of Lot 6 of the Tanzania Standard Gauge Railway (SGR), a 506-km line linking Tabora to Uvinza and onward to the Lake Tanganyika port town of Kigoma. The contract, valued at TSh 7.5 trillion (roughly €2.5 billion, about $2.7 billion), was awarded to a joint venture of China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC) and China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation (CCECC), with construction supervised by the state-owned Tanzania Railways Corporation (TRC).

The route comprises 411 km of main line plus roughly 95 km of station tracks, passing loops and sidings, built to the same 1,435 mm standard gauge as the rest of the network. By the time of the launch ceremony, more than 10% of the works were already complete, with full completion targeted for 2030. Officials project the line will cut the Dar es Salaam–Kigoma journey time from over 20 hours to around 8 hours and create an estimated 15,000 jobs in the Tabora and Kigoma regions, while easing freight costs for the area's mining, agriculture, fisheries and tourism sectors. Lot 6 is designed to connect onward to Lots 7 and 8 — a planned 156 km Uvinza–Burundi border extension and an 84 km Malagarasi–Musongati link inside Burundi — both targeted for completion by 2030-31, extending the Central Corridor toward landlocked Burundi and, eventually, the mineral-rich eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

Lot 6 extends the SGR network westward from the already-operational and under-construction core line between Dar es Salaam and Mwanza, also tracked on this site, which has been built in phases since 2017 with CRCC and other contractors. Tanzania signed its Belt and Road Initiative memorandum of understanding with China in September 2018.

Name: UAE Dubai Holding Headquarters & Jumeirah Residences Emirates Towers (CSCEC Middle East)
Description:
On September 9, 2026, Dubai Holding awarded a AED 5 billion (~$1.36 billion) construction contract — the largest in its history — to China State Construction Engineering Corporation Middle East (CSCEC ME), covering two flagship projects in Dubai's Emirates Towers district: a new Dubai Holding corporate headquarters and the 'Jumeirah Residences Emirates Towers' branded residential development. The signing ceremony was witnessed by Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, and comes as CSCEC ME marks over two decades of operations in the UAE since 2003, having delivered more than 110 large-scale projects across the Gulf.

The headquarters tower is designed by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM) around a circular form with a central open-air atrium and landscaped courtyard, targeting leading international sustainability and workplace-wellbeing standards, with completion slated for 2029. Jumeirah Residences Emirates Towers, developed by Meraas and designed by SCDA Architects, will comprise 754 branded residences across two towers with Arabian-hospitality-style services and wellness amenities, handing over in 2030. Both sit alongside Dubai's existing Emirates Towers complex with connectivity to the city's core business and cultural districts.

The contract extends China's expanding footprint in Gulf real estate and construction following CSCEC's and CCCC-subsidiary China Harbour Engineering Company's roles in the Abu Dhabi–Dubai high-speed rail project, also tracked on this site. The UAE signed its Belt and Road Initiative memorandum of understanding with China in 2018.

Name: Uzbekistan Silk Road Fund Infrastructure Financing Agreement
Description:
On September 9-10, 2026, on the sidelines of the 11th Belt and Road Summit in Hong Kong, Uzbekistan's National Bank for Foreign Economic Activity signed a long-term credit-line financing agreement worth up to $395 million with China's Silk Road Fund — the Chinese state investment vehicle established in 2014 to support Belt and Road projects. The agreement was signed as part of a high-level Uzbek delegation led by Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov.

The financing is earmarked for modernizing Uzbekistan's transport infrastructure, with particular focus on the construction of modern toll expressways; the two sides committed to jointly identify, assess and structure specific infrastructure projects for financing under the framework. The deal supports Uzbekistan's 2026 State Investment Program, which targets $1.5 billion in financing from international financial institutions, and follows the Silk Road Fund's earlier co-investment alongside ACWA Power in Uzbekistan's $1 billion, 1.5 GW Sirdarya gas-fired power project.

The agreement adds to a growing roster of China-Uzbekistan BRI-linked infrastructure, including the China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan Railway and the Angren–Pap electrified railway, both already tracked on this site. Uzbekistan signed its Belt and Road Initiative memorandum of understanding with China in June 2015.

Name: Qatar Bul Hanine Offshore Oil & Gas EPIC Project (COOEC)
Description:
On September 15, 2026, China Offshore Oil Engineering Co., Ltd. (COOEC) — a subsidiary of state-owned China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) — held a steel-cutting ceremony in Qingdao, China, marking the start of fabrication work on a $4 billion Engineering, Procurement, Installation and Commissioning (EPIC) contract for QatarEnergy's Bul Hanine offshore oil field expansion. The contract is described in Chinese and Middle East trade press as the largest overseas offshore oil and gas EPC project ever undertaken by a Chinese company.

The scope of work covers fabrication and installation of more than 130,000 metric tons of steel, over 60 offshore platforms and structures, and roughly 40 subsea pipelines and cables supporting the expansion of the Bul Hanine field, one of QatarEnergy's mature offshore oil assets in the Persian Gulf southeast of Doha. The award extends a long run of Chinese state-owned engineering firms winning large offshore energy contracts in Qatar and the wider Gulf, alongside COOEC's parent CNOOC's broader push into overseas EPC work tied to Belt and Road-linked energy infrastructure financing and contracting.

Name: Rwanda Prince House–Giporoso–Masaka Road (Chinese Government Grant)
Description:
Construction officially launched on September 8, 2026 on a 10.3-kilometre road connecting Prince House and Giporoso to Masaka in Kigali, financed by a grant from the Government of China. The route links the Kigali Special Economic Zone, the Eastern Industrial Zone and the Masaka Medical Complex, and includes a flyover/underpass interchange, new bridges, drainage works and street lighting; part of the corridor is being widened to six lanes.

Rwandan authorities have said they are pushing to compress the originally planned 30-month construction timeline to under 20 months. The project traces its origins to infrastructure commitments made during Chinese President Xi Jinping's 2018 state visit to Rwanda, and adds to a growing roster of Chinese-financed urban road projects in Kigali, including the earlier Masaka-Kabuga Road already tracked on this site. No specific Chinese contractor was named in initial coverage of the groundbreaking.

Name: Vanuatu Port Vila Road Upgrading and Renovation Project (CEEDI)
Description:
On August 10, 2026, Vanuatu and China signed the "Minutes of Discussion for the Professional Site Inspection," a procedural step advancing the Port Vila Road Upgrading and Renovation Project toward implementation. The project is being delivered as Chinese government grant aid (not a commercial loan) through the China Electronic Engineering Design Institute (CEEDI), operating under China's Ministry of Commerce Bureau of International Economic Cooperation.

The project covers the upgrading and sealing of 19 urban roads in Port Vila, Vanuatu's capital, totaling approximately 12.29 kilometres. A specific financial value has not been disclosed in available reporting. This is the first project tracked on this site for Vanuatu, a Belt and Road Initiative signatory, and reflects China's continued grant-aid engagement with Pacific Island nations following a string of earlier China-funded infrastructure and public-building projects in the country.

Name: Egypt Linglong Tire Manufacturing Complex (Linglong Group)
Description:
The Linglong Tire Manufacturing Complex is a $2 billion Chinese private-sector investment announced during Xi Jinping's state visit to Egypt on September 2-3, 2026 — his first visit to the country in a decade — and the largest single addition yet to Egypt's fast-growing cluster of Chinese tyre manufacturing plants. On September 6, 2026, Linglong Group vice chairman Wang Lin and Egypt's Industry Minister Khaled Hashem signed the memorandum of understanding in the presence of Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, committing Linglong to build an integrated tyre and rubber products complex at Borg El Arab, west of Alexandria, on a site of up to 3 million square metres.

The complex will manufacture passenger car tyres, truck and bus tyres, industrial/equipment tyres, conveyor belts, and supporting materials including carbon black and steel cord, and is projected to create more than 5,000 jobs. Egypt currently imports close to 8 million tyres a year at a cost of roughly $1.25 billion, and the government has pitched the project — alongside Egyptian partner Nile Trading and Supplies (parent of the Fit & Fix brand) — as the anchor of a new integrated automotive-tyre value chain aimed largely at export markets in Europe, the United States and the Gulf. The deal follows preliminary talks that began in April 2026 and makes Linglong the latest of several Chinese tyre majors — alongside Zhongce Rubber (ZC Rubber), which already operates a $500 million complex in Egypt — to commit to large-scale manufacturing investment in the country, which signed its Belt and Road Initiative MoU with China in January 2016.

Name: Kenya Jomo Kenyatta International Airport Modernization (CRBC)
Description:
On June 23, 2026, the Government of Kenya and China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) signed a contract to modernise Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA), Kenya's main international gateway in Nairobi, in a deal valued at KSh154.2 billion (approximately $1.2 billion). The agreement was signed by Kenya Airports Authority and Principal Secretary for Transport Teresia Mbaika on the government side and CRBC General Manager Yu Xiaodong on the contractor's side, following a three-month procurement process that drew more than 40 companies into pre-bid discussions after the JKIA Master Plan was completed in February 2026.

The project is structured around three main components: construction of a new terminal building and associated support facilities, modernisation and upgrade of existing airport infrastructure, and improvements to airside and landside operations intended to raise JKIA's operational efficiency and service levels. Lebanese engineering firm Dar Al-Handasah has been appointed to provide supervisory and design-review services for the works. The award makes CRBC — already Kenya's dominant Chinese infrastructure contractor through projects such as the Nairobi Expressway — one of the country's single largest holders of Chinese-financed construction contracts, with its cumulative Kenyan contract book reported to exceed KSh1.2 trillion following the JKIA award. Kenya, which signed a Belt and Road cooperation agreement with China in 2017, has not disclosed the financing arrangement for the JKIA contract as of this writing.
